fact_sheet.guest_policy: All guests aged 12+ need a ticket; RSVP required. The documents do not state complimentary admission, VIP access, or travel support for speakers, panelists, or other invited guests; do not promise these. Sponsorship benefits apply to sponsors at the stated tiers, not generally to invited guests.
fact_sheet.budget_basis: No working budget or overall cost cap is stated. The tracker says Golden Phoenix will provide dinner for 200, so use 200 attendees as a planning proxy and an assumed $150 all-in event cost per attendee for a gala dinner in New Haven: 200 × $150 = $30,000. This is a rough gross-cost estimate, not a documented budget; the donated dinner may lower cash costs, and venue pricing is not provided. The expense sheet lists individual expenses, not a total event budget.

key_messages: The gala is organized by Harbor Lights Community Association in New Haven.
The invitation states that proceeds will go entirely to the youth after-school tutoring program.
The evening program includes a reception and lion dance, welcome, keynote, community service recognition, and a guest-of-honor toast.
The invitation asks Dr. Grace Wong to speak about community health stories.

conflicts.reason: The tracker, planning notes, and invitation agree on May 15; the sponsorship package appears to retain an earlier date. Confirm the package is corrected before reuse.

Keynote speaker — New Haven-area educator, youth-program leader, or community advocate with relevant after-school tutoring experience; contingency if Dr. Grace Wong declines or remains unavailable.
Guest-of-honor toast — Local community leader or youth-education supporter who could deliver a concise ceremonial toast; scout only if Prof. Weilin Huang is unavailable.

Lighthouse sponsor — New Haven-area credit union or community-minded business with capacity for a USD 5,000 sponsorship; identify an alternate prospect while Pacific Harbor Credit Union’s board decision is pending.

Dear Dr. Raman,

We’re looking forward to welcoming you as the keynote speaker at Yale SOM Energy Club — Clean Energy Conference 2027 on Friday, March 26, 2027. Your keynote is scheduled for 9:15 AM at Evans Hall, Yale School of Management, 165 Whitney Avenue, New Haven, CT 06511. As noted in our invitation, we’ll cover travel from Boston and one hotel night, and we’d be glad to host you at the reception. Could you share your preferred travel timing and any details we should know to coordinate the travel and hotel? We’ll confirm the arrangements with you before booking.

Hannah Becker

The club’s planning materials list panels on climate investing, consumer brands going global, and AI and technology supply chains, followed by a gala dinner.

fact_sheet.guest_policy: Registration is required for everyone; each registered attendee may bring one guest, who must register in advance under their own name. Gala dinner is capped at 150 seats and is ticketed. Speaker-specific arrangements documented: Catherine Lau is offered economy-class airfare from Hong Kong and two hotel nights; Jiaming Lin's travel and lodging will be assisted with details in an itinerary. No other speaker travel or honorarium terms are specified in the current documents.
fact_sheet.budget_basis: No working budget or total cost cap is stated; the finance sheet lists individual expenses, not an event budget. Estimate: 300 expected attendees × $100 per attendee for conference food, materials and general event costs = $30,000; 150 gala seats × $100 incremental dinner cost = $15,000; $5,000 estimated AV/production; and $4,000 estimated speaker travel/lodging assistance for a small number of out-of-town speakers. Total = $54,000. This is a rough planning assumption, not a confirmed cost or commitment.

drafts.subject: Could you introduce us to Chris Miller about our summit panel?
drafts.body:
Dear Prof. Huang,

I hope you’re well. Would you be comfortable introducing us to Chris Miller? We’re putting together Panel C on AI & Tech Supply Chains for the Yale SOM Greater China Club — US–China Business Summit 2027, and would value the chance to check whether he might be interested and available. Before sending a formal invitation, we’d also like to confirm his current affiliation.

For convenience, here’s a short note you could forward:

“Dear Chris,

The Yale SOM Greater China Club is planning Panel C, ‘AI & Tech Supply Chains,’ at its US–China Business Summit 2027 on Saturday, April 10, at Evans Hall, Yale School of Management, 165 Whitney Avenue, New Haven, CT 06511. We’re exploring a panel discussion on semiconductor ecosystems and the strategic implications of the chip supply chain. Would you be open to a brief conversation about the possibility of joining, and could you let us know your current affiliation and availability?

Best,
Yale SOM Greater China Club”

No worries at all if an introduction isn’t convenient. Thank you for considering it.

Best,
Yale SOM Greater China Club
team@gcsummit-yale.example.org

documents.text:
# Research memo — Responsible AI in Global Business Conference 2027

The Responsible AI in Global Business Conference is the Yale School of Management Artificial Intelligence Association’s flagship, multidisciplinary conference. The organiser’s note says to plan on early-to-mid April 2027 at Yale SOM’s Evans Hall, but that date and venue are not yet confirmed in a published 2027 announcement; treat them as assumptions, not event facts. Recent editions brought together business, academic, policy and Yale-community audiences, with a full-day format of keynotes, panels and breakout discussions. The conference spans AI technology and business adoption, management, societal impact, policy and regulation.

## Facts (with sources)
- 2027 date: Not announced in the conference’s published page. Early-to-mid April 2027 is an organiser-provided planning assumption, not independently published or confirmed. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/)
- 2027 venue: Not announced for 2027. Yale SOM’s Evans Hall in New Haven is the organiser-provided planning assumption; the 2026 edition was held at Yale SOM. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/)
- Organiser: Yale School of Management Artificial Intelligence Association (AI Association), described as the conference’s host/flagship event organiser. The 2025 edition also listed Y-SIM and the Data & Trust Alliance as co-organisers. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/; https://som.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2025-03/Yale2025ResponsibleAIConferenceAgenda0317forUpload.pdf)
- Website: Conference page, currently presenting the 2026 edition and 2026 sponsors; no 2027 event details were found. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/)
- Registration/ticket prices: 2026 conference page displays general and Yale registration links, but no prices were visible in the accessible published page. 2027 registration and pricing were not found. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/)
- Audience size: The 2026 organizers reported over 300 registrants. A 2025 news report anticipated over 400 in-person participants and 300–400 virtual attendees; the 2025 agenda document says 400 attendees. These are edition-specific figures and not a 2027 forecast. (https://som.yale.edu/story/2026/moving-smart-and-breaking-less-responsible-ai-global-business-conference; https://yaledailynews.com/articles/yale-to-host-global-leaders-conference-on-responsible-ai-in-business; https://som.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2025-03/Yale2025ResponsibleAIConferenceAgenda0317forUpload.pdf)
- Tracks/agenda: The 2026 page describes a multidisciplinary focus on technology, management, societal impact, policy and regulation. Published 2026 panels covered consumer protection and product safety, workforce and automation, AI investment/capital efficiency, and embodied AI/robotics; breakout sessions included AI startups and advertising. (https://groups.som.yale.edu/aia/conference/; https://groups.som.yale.edu/AIA/agenda/)
- Recent-edition format: The 2026 event was a daylong conference at Evans Hall with panels; event listings describe keynotes, panels and breakout discussions. The 2025 edition was listed for April 3, 2025, 8 a.m.–6 p.m., at Evans Hall, 165 Whitney Avenue, New Haven. (https://som.yale.edu/story/2026/moving-smart-and-breaking-less-responsible-ai-global-business-conference; https://www.wshu.org/community-calendar/event/2026-responsible-ai-in-global-business-conference-27-03-2026-16-55-19; https://som.yale.edu/event/responsible-ai-global-business-2025)
- Potential Yale AI intermediary: Tauhid Zaman is identified by a Yale SOM source as associate professor of operations management and special advisor for SOM’s AI initiative. This is a potential routing lead, not confirmation of his 2027 event role. (https://poetsandquants.com/2026/06/17/to-turn-managers-into-builders-yale-som-makes-over-its-mba-core/)

## Past speakers
- Sarah Bird — Chief Product Officer of Responsible AI, Microsoft (2025) (https://som.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2025-03/Yale2025ResponsibleAIConferenceAgenda0317forUpload.pdf)

documents.text:
# Research memo — MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference 2027 — Research Memo

The MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference (SSAC) is an annual, in-person forum for sports-industry professionals, researchers, students, and fans to discuss analytics, business, and technology in sports. The conference is chaired by co-founders Jessica Gelman and Daryl Morey and organized by MIT Sloan students. The organizer-provided 2027 dates and venue are corroborated by the conference’s Eventbrite listing; as of this research, the official site says 2027 speakers are still forthcoming. The latest completed edition was SSAC26, held March 6–7, 2026, with more than 2,500 attendees. The organizer’s desired 2027 topics—keynotes, sports analytics, AI, betting markets, and sponsors—are planning notes, not a published 2027 agenda.

## Facts (with sources)
- 2027 date: February 25–26, 2027 (Thursday–Friday), according to the 2027 Eventbrite listing: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-2027-tickets-1991125033575
- 2027 venue: Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center, 415 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-2027-tickets-1991125033575
- Organiser: MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference; chaired by co-founders Jessica Gelman and Daryl Morey, and organized by MIT Sloan students: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/about/faqs
- Official website: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/
- Registration: the official site links to 2027 ticket sales, but a verifiable 2027 ticket price was not available in the pages reviewed: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/
- Audience: more than 2,500 people attended the 2026 edition, including coaches and players from Team USA, NBA, WNBA, and other organizations: https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310
- 2027 tracks/agenda: no specific 2027 agenda or track list located; the official site says to stay tuned for 2027 speakers. The conference describes its overall scope as sports analytics, business, and technology: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/speakers ; https://www.sloansportsconference.com/
- Most recent completed edition (2026): March 6–7, 2026, at Menino Conference and Exhibition Center; official archive lists 300 program items, including panels, events, and research papers: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference
- 2026 program themes included investment in sports, the sports ticket economy, innovation in leagues, hockey and basketball analytics, AI in sports, and gambling/tanking issues: https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference ; https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310

## Past speakers
- Adam Silver — Commissioner, NBA (2026; conversation on basketball, tanking, and gambling) (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)
- Sue Bird — Basketball Hall of Famer and 2026 conversation moderator (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)
- John Donahoe — Athletic Director, Stanford Athletics (2026) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference)
- Megan Rapinoe — Soccer legend, activist, author, and co-founder of A Touch More (2026) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference)
- Jason Robins — Co-Founder, CEO and Board Chairman, DraftKings (2026) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference)
- Nate Silver — Statistician, author, and founder of Silver Bulletin (2026) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2026-conference)
- A’ja Wilson — Las Vegas Aces forward, entrepreneur, and author (2025) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2025-conference)
- David Blitzer — Co-Founder and Co-Managing Partner, Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (2025) (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/conference/2025-conference)

## Past sponsors
- Wasserman Foundation — 2026 Hackathon presenter (https://www.sloansportsconference.com/hackathon)

## Organiser team (public)
- Jessica Gelman — Co-Chair; CEO, Kraft Analytics Group (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)
- Daryl Morey — Co-Chair; President of Basketball Operations, Philadelphia 76ers (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)
- Mike O’Connell — Co-Lead (2026) (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)
- Patrick Scheri — Co-Lead (2026) (https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-sloan-sports-analytics-conference-shows-why-data-makes-difference-0310)

## Not found (to be estimated)
- 2027 speaker and keynote lineup, including whether any speakers are confirmed.
- 2027 agenda, named tracks, and session descriptions; specifically no announced sessions dedicated to AI or betting markets found.
- 2027 ticket prices and detailed ticket tiers; ticket sales are linked from the official site, but pricing was not verifiable in reviewed pages.
- 2027 sponsor roster, sponsor tiers, available inventory, and sponsorship prices; only the 2026 Hackathon presenter above was confirmed in reviewed official sources.
- Event budget, speaker honoraria, travel support, and other guest benefits.

## Organiser notes
February 25-26, 2027, Thomas M. Menino Convention and Exhibition Center, Boston. We need keynote speakers, panelists across sports analytics, AI and betting markets, and sponsors.

Best,
MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference team
